newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico approves voter list, opposition protests.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approves voter list, opposition protests.

text.p: Mexico's top electoral authority approved a voter registration list on Tuesday for next month's congressional elections despite opposition complaints that it had flaws that could facilitate fraud.

The Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) approved a list of 52.2 million voters for the July 6 elections. Another 813,744 people were excluded because they had not picked up their voter credential by last January's deadline.

Mexicans will elect a new lower house and a quarter of the senate next month. Interest has been high because President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) could lose its lower house majority for the first time ever.
Six state governors and the first elected mayor of Mexico City will also be voted in on the same day.

IFE president Jose Woldenberg said he was convinced the voting list was reliable but left-wingers sharply attacked the data, saying more than 10 million people were registered in areas where they did not live.
Jose Barberan, a leader of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), said the list of electors was "much worse than the 1994 one" when Mexico held presidential elections.
He said the mistakes in the list did not necessarily mean there would definitely be fraud but added that they would "make it easier".
Clara Jusidman, the head of the Federal Electoral Register, told reporters that Mexico's list of voters compared favourably with the best of any other in the world.

She admitted that 20 percent of voters -- or 10 million people -- were not registered with their correct address but said this was "normal" because they had moved house without notifying the authorities.
The IFE also slapped fines worth the equivalent of $1,300 on Mexico's two biggest political parties for insulting each other.

The PRI was fined after its official newspaper La Republica printed pictures of conservative National Action Party (PAN) leader Felipe Calderon wearing a swastika armband and standing next to Adolf Hitler.
The PAN was fined for saying that PRI candidates had grown rich through dishonesty and had made money out of the poverty of the Mexican people.
